title: Mock 4 · Investor Services Focus
blurb: Extra weight on transactions, payments, KYC and disclosures, the chapters that carry the most marks.

questions.q: An investor in bonds differs from investors in equity, real estate and commodities mainly because the bond investor:
options: Has lent money and the receipts (interest and principal) are agreed at issue
Is a part-owner of the business
questions.explanation: Bonds are lending assets with agreed cash flows. Equity, real estate and commodities are ownership assets whose future receipts are uncertain.

questions.q: An investor in gold or silver can expect returns only in the form of:
questions.explanation: Commodities like gold and silver generate no current income; the investor relies only on capital appreciation.

questions.q: An overnight fund invests in securities having a maturity of:
questions.explanation: Overnight funds invest in overnight securities with a maturity of 1 day.
hints: That is a money market fund.
That is the ultra-short duration band.

questions.q: Life Cycle Funds may be launched with tenures that are:
options: Between 5 and 30 years, in multiples of 5 years
questions.explanation: Life Cycle Funds have a minimum tenure of 5 years and a maximum of 30, in multiples of 5. A mutual fund can have at most 6 active for subscription at a time.
hints: That range describes target maturity funds.

questions.q: An AMC may offer more than one scheme in the same category in which of these cases?
options: Large cap funds with different fund managers
Liquid funds with different minimum amounts
questions.explanation: Only one scheme per category is allowed, except index funds/ETFs on different indices, FoFs with different underlying schemes and sector/thematic funds on different sectors or themes.

questions.q: To keep the function independent, the Compliance Officer of an AMC reports directly to:
questions.explanation: The Compliance Officer reports directly to the head of the AMC, works closely with the trustees and must report any non-compliance directly and immediately to the trustees.

questions.q: Which agencies has AMFI appointed to provide the valuation matrix for non-traded or thinly traded debt securities?
questions.explanation: SEBI requires at least two valuation agencies; AMFI appointed CRISIL Ltd. and ICRA Ltd.

questions.q: As a Life Cycle Fund moves closer to its target maturity date, its asset allocation typically:
options: Moves out of equity into debt along a glide path
questions.explanation: Life Cycle Funds reduce risk over time through a glide path: the equity share comes down and debt goes up as maturity approaches.
hints: The opposite of a glide path.
Gold is only one of several asset classes.

questions.q: What is the main driver of returns in a Fixed Maturity Plan?
options: Yield on the debt securities held
questions.explanation: In liquid, money market funds and FMPs, returns come mainly from the yield on the debt instruments.
hints: That drives equity and index funds.

questions.q: By when must the Statement of Additional Information (SAI) be updated each year?
options: Within 3 months of the end of the financial year
questions.explanation: The SAI is updated regularly by the end of 3 months of every financial year; material changes are updated on an ongoing basis.
hints: That is the KIM/SID update cycle.

questions.q: How often must AMCs disclose the Total Expense Ratio (TER) of their schemes on their own and AMFI's websites?
questions.explanation: AMCs must prominently disclose TER daily, scheme-wise and date-wise (except infrastructure debt fund schemes).

questions.q: In the Key Information Memorandum, the performance of the scheme and its benchmark is shown for which periods?
options: 1 year, 3 years, 5 years and since inception
questions.explanation: The KIM shows scheme and benchmark performance over the last 1, 3 and 5 years and since inception.

questions.q: AMCs must carry out due diligence on distributors who, among other criteria, have a presence in more than how many locations?
questions.explanation: Criteria (any one): multiple points of presence (more than 20 locations), AUM over ₹100 crore in the non-institutional category, commission over ₹1 crore p.a. industry-wide, or over ₹50 lakh from a single MF.

questions.q: A distributor invests his own savings in a scheme using his ARN. Is commission payable on this investment?
options: No; no commission is payable on self-business
Yes, at double the normal rate
Only if the amount exceeds ₹1 lakh
questions.explanation: Commission is paid for mobilising money from clients, so no commission is payable on the distributor's own investments.
hints: Upfront commission is not allowed anyway.

questions.q: Rahul invested ₹50,000 at NAV ₹10 (5,000 units). He received an IDCW of ₹1 per unit, and the NAV is now ₹11. What is his total return?
For an index fund, a lower tracking error indicates that:
options: The fund's returns are closer to those of the index
The fund outperforms the index by a wide margin
questions.explanation: Tracking error is the annualised SD of the return difference between the index fund and its index. The lower it is, the more closely the fund tracks the index.
hints: Higher costs tend to increase tracking error.
Index funds aim to mirror, not beat, the index.

questions.q: Who selects the benchmark for an actively managed mutual fund scheme?
options: The AMC in consultation with the trustees
questions.explanation: Benchmark selection is decided by the AMC in consultation with the trustees, and the chosen benchmark must be mentioned in the SID.
hints: SEBI sets principles, not specific benchmarks.

questions.q: A resident individual receives IDCW of ₹15,000 from a scheme in a year. What TDS applies?
questions.explanation: TDS at 10% applies to IDCW from mutual funds, even for residents, if the amount exceeds ₹10,000.
hints: Residents have no TDS on redemptions, but IDCW above ₹10,000 attracts TDS.

questions.q: A long-term capital loss can be set off against:
questions.explanation: Long-term capital loss can be set off only against long-term capital gains. Short-term capital loss can be set off against both STCG and LTCG.
hints: Capital losses can't be set off against other heads.

questions.q: Which third-party payment is acceptable for a mutual fund purchase?
options: A friend paying ₹2 lakh for an adult investor
A grandparent paying ₹40,000 for a grandchild who is a minor, with a third-party declaration
A demand draft bought with ₹60,000 cash
A cheque from an unrelated company
questions.explanation: Parents, grandparents or related persons may pay on behalf of a minor (love and affection / gift) up to ₹50,000 per purchase or SIP instalment, with KYC and a third-party declaration.
hints: DDs issued against cash of ₹50,000 or more are not accepted.

questions.q: Which of these investors is exempt from providing a PAN for mutual fund investments?
questions.explanation: PAN-exempt categories include Sikkim residents, government transactions, court-appointed officials, UN/multilateral bodies and micro-investments up to ₹50,000 per year per mutual fund. They still provide alternate photo ID.
hints: PAN is the sole identification for NRI KYC.

questions.q: Under the multiple bank account facility, an individual investor can register up to how many bank accounts with a mutual fund?
questions.explanation: Individuals can register up to five bank accounts and non-individuals up to ten, with one designated as the default account.
hints: That is the limit for non-individuals.

questions.q: An investor puts ₹25,000 into an open-ended scheme where the applicable NAV is ₹12.50. Ignoring stamp duty, how many units are allotted?
questions.explanation: Units = Amount ÷ Sale price (= NAV, since entry load is banned) = 25,000 ÷ 12.50 = 2,000.

questions.q: Under the AMFI Code of Ethics, a 'significant unit holder' is an entity holding at least what share of a scheme's total corpus?
questions.explanation: A significant unit holder holds 5% or more of the total corpus of any scheme, including entities it controls.

questions.q: A scheme launched 4 months ago wants to advertise its performance. What does the SEBI code allow?
options: No past performance can be shown
questions.explanation: Where a scheme has existed for less than six months, past performance shall not be provided (liquid, overnight and money market funds have a separate short-period yield rule).
